summary: A valley vista in the village country south of Ahwa — green bowls, field terraces and forest ridges where almost nobody stops.
description:
The Wasurna valley is the south-western pocket's open moment: village fields and terraces falling into a green bowl, forest ridges behind, and a mapped vantage where the road crests enough to take it all in. In monsoon the composition is the district's classic — moving cloud, saturated paddy, dark ridgelines — without a single stall or signboard to share it with.

It earns twenty minutes on any south-western loop, longer if the light is doing something. The Temburgartha dam's sunset ridge is a short drive north; the Chikhalda falls pocket is just west.
highlights: Open valley vista in a district of closed forest
Links the dam ridge to the Chikhalda falls pocket

modes.road: The Wasurna village road south from Ahwa; the vantage is at the road's high point
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

visit.notes: A pause, not a destination — combine with the pocket's falls.

seasonality.notes: Monsoon for the drama, early winter for clarity; brown by late spring.

experience.photography_notes: Wide frames at golden hour; the terraces give leading lines the forest belt never offers.

warnings: Park fully off the carriageway — the road is narrow

tips: Chikhalda pocket in the morning, the valley late, dam ridge for sunset — the full south-western day
Respect the fields — the terraces are working farmland
